item.content:encoded:
If you are a development, international relations, communications, public policy, or partnerships professional looking for an opportunity with the United Nations system, UNICEF is inviting applications for a Partnerships Officer, NO-1, Fixed-Term Appointment in Pretoria, South Africa.

This position offers an opportunity to contribute to UNICEF’s work in South Africa by supporting strategic partnerships, resource mobilization, stakeholder engagement, policy influence, research, and coordination. The successful candidate will work within the UNICEF South Africa Country Office and contribute to efforts aimed at strengthening investments and opportunities for children.

The position is particularly relevant for professionals with experience in partnership management, donor relations, resource mobilization, stakeholder engagement, communications, programme management, international development, or policy analysis.

Application deadline: August 28, 2026, South Africa Standard Time.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organization: UNICEF
  • Position: Partnerships Officer
  • Job Number: 595114
  • Vacancy Reference: #00137970
  • Position Level: NO-1
  • Contract Type: Fixed-Term Appointment
  • Duty Station: Pretoria, South Africa
  • Functional Area: Partnerships
  • Country: South Africa
  • Advertised: August 14, 2026
  • Deadline: August 28, 2026
  • Required Experience: At least 1 year of relevant professional experience
  • Minimum Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent first-level university degree
  • Working Language: English

About UNICEF

UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories around the world to protect children’s rights, save children’s lives, and help children reach their full potential from early childhood through adolescence.

The organization describes its work as more than simply employment, emphasizing a commitment to promoting the rights of every child. UNICEF also provides staff with opportunities for professional and personal development within a diverse and purpose-driven working environment.

The Partnerships Officer position is located within the UNICEF South Africa Country Office in Pretoria and reports to the Chief of Partnerships, Advocacy and Communication.

The role supports UNICEF’s broader mission while contributing specifically to partnership development, resource mobilization, information analysis, stakeholder engagement, and policy influence in South Africa.

About the Investing in Children Programme

The Partnerships Officer will support the Investing in Children programme component, which focuses on strengthening strategic partnerships, mobilizing resources, and advancing equitable opportunities for children in South Africa.

The programme seeks to:

  • Strengthen strategic partnerships
  • Mobilize additional resources for children
  • Promote equitable opportunities
  • Explore innovative financing approaches
  • Improve the use of existing investments
  • Ensure value for money
  • Support impact at scale
  • Contribute to measurable and sustainable results for children

The programme also supports the effective implementation of the UNICEF South Africa Country Programme Document (CPD) 2026–2030.

The broader objective is to ensure that investments in children translate into measurable, equitable, and sustainable outcomes.

What Does a Partnerships Officer at UNICEF Do?

The Partnerships Officer will provide research, analytical, coordination, and partnership support to Partnership Specialists and senior management.

The position involves helping UNICEF understand its external environment, strengthen relationships with stakeholders, identify opportunities, and improve the organization’s ability to mobilize resources.

The successful candidate will be expected to gather, analyze, and report information in ways that produce useful, evidence-based insights.

This information will help UNICEF:

  • Understand its partners and stakeholders
  • Strengthen partner relationships
  • Identify potential funding opportunities
  • Support discussions with partners
  • Improve internal information sharing
  • Monitor partnership progress
  • Contribute to resource mobilization
  • Support policy influence
  • Increase UNICEF’s visibility
  • Strengthen organizational credibility

Accurate and timely information is particularly important because strong communication with partners can help build trust and strengthen UNICEF’s ability to secure additional resources.

The position will therefore play an important supporting role in helping senior management and partnership teams identify and pursue opportunities that can contribute to UNICEF’s mission.

Key Areas of Responsibility

1. Partnership Support

The Partnerships Officer will assist Partnership Specialists and senior management in their engagement with key stakeholders.

This may involve supporting:

  • Partner relationship management
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Partnership coordination
  • Communication with external partners
  • Internal coordination around partnerships
  • Monitoring partnership developments

The officer will help ensure that relevant information about stakeholders and partnerships is captured and shared appropriately within the organization.

2. Research and Environmental Scanning

The position requires the ability to gather and analyze information about the external environment.

This includes identifying developments that could affect UNICEF’s partnerships, funding opportunities, policy engagement, and strategic priorities.

The officer will need to turn information into fact-based insights that can support decision-making.

Strong research and analytical skills are therefore important for this position.

3. Resource Mobilization

Resource mobilization is another significant component of the position.

The Partnerships Officer will contribute to identifying and supporting opportunities that could generate additional resources for UNICEF’s work.

This can include supporting:

  • Fundraising efforts
  • Donor engagement
  • Partnership development
  • Funding opportunity analysis
  • Proposal development
  • Donor reporting
  • Communication with potential partners

Applicants with previous experience in fundraising or resource mobilization may therefore have an advantage.

4. Stakeholder Engagement

The successful candidate will contribute to UNICEF’s engagement with key stakeholders.

This requires strong communication, networking, relationship-building, and coordination abilities.

The role may involve interacting with different groups, including donors, development partners, government stakeholders, private-sector organizations, and other relevant actors.

5. Policy Influence and Analysis

The position also contributes to policy influence.

The Partnerships Officer will support the gathering and analysis of information that can help UNICEF engage in substantive discussions with partners and stakeholders.

Applicants with experience in policy analysis, international development, public policy, international relations, or related areas may find this aspect particularly relevant.

Minimum Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet the minimum requirements established by UNICEF for the position.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must have a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent first-level university degree.

Relevant academic fields include:

  • International Studies
  • Political Science
  • Communications
  • International Development
  • International Relations
  • Public Policy
  • Other closely related disciplines

Candidates whose academic background is in a related field may also be considered where their education is relevant to the responsibilities of the position.

Professional Experience

Applicants are required to have at least one year of relevant work experience.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Programme management
  • Partnership management
  • Resource mobilization
  • Donor relations
  • External relations
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Interagency coordination
  • Policy analysis
  • International development
  • Communications
  • Other related areas

This means the position is not strictly limited to candidates who have previously held the exact title of “Partnerships Officer.”

Professionals with relevant experience across the areas above may be able to demonstrate the required competencies.

Required Skills

UNICEF identifies several important skill areas for this position, including:

  • Resource mobilization
  • Negotiation
  • Networking
  • Communication
  • Development

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate strong interpersonal and professional communication skills, as well as the ability to build relationships and work collaboratively with different stakeholders.

Language Requirement

Fluency in English is required.

Knowledge of additional languages is considered an asset.

UNICEF specifically identifies knowledge of another official UN language as desirable. These include:

  • Arabic
  • Chinese
  • French
  • Russian
  • Spanish

Knowledge of at least one additional official local language is also considered an asset.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

While not necessarily mandatory, UNICEF identifies several additional qualifications and experiences that could strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Fundraising and Partnership Management

Experience in fundraising and managing partnerships would be beneficial.

UNICEF or UN Experience

Previous experience working with UNICEF or the broader United Nations system would be an advantage.

Private-Sector Knowledge

Knowledge of the private-sector landscape in South Africa would also be valuable.

Donor Communication

Experience communicating with donors is desirable.

Proposal and Report Writing

Applicants with experience drafting:

  • Funding proposals
  • Donor reports
  • Partnership documentation

may have an advantage.

Donor Field Visits

Experience leading or coordinating field visits involving donors is also considered desirable.

Country-Level Development Experience

Relevant experience at country level, particularly in:

  • Development
  • Fragile settings
  • Humanitarian contexts

would be advantageous.

UNICEF Core Values

Applicants should understand that technical qualifications are only one part of working for UNICEF.

UNICEF’s core values include:

  • Care
  • Respect
  • Integrity
  • Trust
  • Accountability
  • Sustainability

These values are reflected in UNICEF’s organizational culture and expectations for its employees.

UNICEF Competencies Required for the Position

UNICEF identifies seven competencies particularly relevant to this position:

  1. Builds and maintains partnerships
  2. Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness
  3. Drives to achieve results for impact
  4. Innovates and embraces change
  5. Manages ambiguity and complexity
  6. Thinks and acts strategically
  7. Works collaboratively with others

Applicants should therefore demonstrate more than academic qualifications. Their application should also show evidence of partnership-building, strategic thinking, collaboration, ethical conduct, adaptability, and the ability to deliver results.

Who Can Apply?

This is a national officer position based in South Africa, and UNICEF specifically states that eligible and suitable national candidates are encouraged to apply.

The position is based in Pretoria, South Africa, and UNICEF’s vacancy notice includes a visa and residence requirement stating that UNICEF will not facilitate the issuance of a visa and work authorization for candidates under consideration for National Officer and General Service positions.

Therefore, applicants should carefully consider their eligibility to work in South Africa before applying.

The opportunity is open to qualified candidates without discrimination based on race, nationality, gender, religion, disability, socioeconomic background, or other protected characteristics, subject to the position’s eligibility and work authorization requirements.

APPLY HERE 

People Who Are Most Likely to Qualify

The strongest candidates are likely to be professionals who have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline
  • At least one year of relevant professional experience
  • Strong English-language skills
  • Experience with partnerships or stakeholder engagement
  • Experience in resource mobilization or fundraising
  • Strong communication and networking abilities
  • Experience in development, international relations, policy, or communications
  • The ability to conduct research and analyze information
  • An understanding of donor relationships and external engagement

Candidates with additional UN experience, fundraising experience, proposal-writing experience, donor communication experience, or knowledge of the South African private sector may have an additional advantage.

Important Information About UNICEF Recruitment

UNICEF emphasizes that it does not charge applicants any processing fee at any stage of recruitment.

Applicants should not be asked to pay a fee for:

  • Submitting an application
  • Taking an interview
  • Validation
  • Appointment
  • Training

UNICEF also states that it will not ask applicants for their bank account information during the recruitment process.

Applicants should therefore be cautious of anyone claiming to represent UNICEF and requesting payment or sensitive financial information.

Background Checks and Other Conditions

Successful candidates will be subject to UNICEF’s recruitment requirements, which include rigorous reference and background checks.

These checks can include verification of:

  • Academic credentials
  • Employment history
  • Professional references

Selected candidates may also be required to provide additional information as part of the background-check process.

UNICEF appointments are also subject to medical clearance.

Other requirements may apply depending on the candidate and the conditions of the appointment.

Humanitarian Deployment

Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF’s Strategic Plan.

As a result, UNICEF notes that staff members at all levels and across functional areas may be called upon to support humanitarian responses.

This means successful candidates may potentially be expected to contribute to humanitarian operations when required, including efforts that strengthen community resilience and national response capacity.

Important Note for Government Employees

Government employees who are selected for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up a UNICEF assignment.

Applicants currently employed by government institutions should therefore take this requirement into consideration.

How to Apply for the UNICEF Partnerships Officer Position

Interested and qualified applicants should submit their application through the official UNICEF recruitment system.

Applicants should carefully review the complete job description and ensure that their education, professional experience, skills, and other qualifications are accurately reflected in their application.

Application deadline: August 28, 2026, South Africa Standard Time.

Apply for the UNICEF Partnerships Officer position

Applicants are encouraged to apply before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Full Job Description

UNICEF has provided a complete job description for applicants who want to understand the responsibilities and requirements of the position in greater detail.

Download the Full Partnerships Officer Job Description

For additional information about UNICEF careers and job categories, applicants can consult the official UNICEF careers resources.

UNICEF Careers

Why This Opportunity Is Worth Considering

The Partnerships Officer position could be particularly valuable for professionals who want to develop a career at the intersection of international development, partnerships, resource mobilization, communications, and child-focused development.

Working within UNICEF would provide exposure to a major international development organization and opportunities to engage with a wide range of stakeholders.

The position also offers the chance to contribute to UNICEF’s efforts to strengthen investments in children and support equitable and sustainable development outcomes in South Africa.

For professionals interested in partnerships and development, the role could provide valuable experience in:

  • Strategic partnership development
  • Resource mobilization
  • Donor relations
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Policy analysis
  • International development
  • Communications
  • Research and analysis
  • Interagency coordination
  • Programme support

Visit HERE to learn more about the NICEF Partnerships Officer, NO-1, Fixed-Term Job in Pretoria, South Africa

Conclusion

The UNICEF Partnerships Officer, NO-1, Fixed-Term Appointment in Pretoria, South Africa is an opportunity for qualified professionals with a background in international development, international relations, communications, public policy, political science, partnerships, or related disciplines.

Applicants need at least a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent first-level university qualification and one year of relevant professional experience, along with fluency in English. Experience in fundraising, partnerships, donor communication, proposal writing, development, or the UN system can further strengthen an application.

The position will contribute to UNICEF’s efforts to build strategic partnerships, mobilize resources, improve stakeholder engagement, and support better outcomes for children in South Africa.

If your academic background and professional experience align with the requirements, carefully review the full job description and submit your application through UNICEF’s official recruitment platform before August 28, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
BRAC, one of the world’s leading development organisations, is inviting applications for several Regular Internship opportunities in 2026 across different departments and programmes. These internships provide students, recent graduates and other qualified candidates with an opportunity to gain practical professional experience while contributing to the work of a globally recognised development organisation.

The current BRAC internship openings cover areas including Human Resources, executive support, microfinance, climate action, technology, finance and accounts. The internships are particularly relevant for candidates who want to build careers in international development, nonprofit management, finance, technology, human resources, climate and sustainability, operations, and related fields.

Importantly, this updated list includes only internship opportunities whose application deadlines have not yet passed as of August 20, 2026. Opportunities with deadlines of August 18, August 19 and August 20, 2026 have been excluded because their application periods have already closed.

BRAC Regular Internship 2026: Current Opportunities

The following BRAC internship opportunities remain open for applications:

  1. BRAC International – Talent Acquisition, Human Resources
    • Application deadline: August 22, 2026
  2. BRAC International – Executive Director’s Office
    • Application deadline: August 22, 2026
  3. Microfinance – Progoti
    • Application deadline: August 24, 2026
  4. Climate Bridge Fund (CBF) Secretariat
    • Application deadline: August 26, 2026
  5. Microfinance – Operational Strategy and Implementation (Dabi)
    • Application deadline: August 26, 2026
  6. Technology – IT HelpDesk
    • Application deadline: August 29, 2026
  7. Finance and Accounts – Treasury
    • Application deadline: August 31, 2026

Because these deadlines are approaching quickly, interested applicants should review the individual internship descriptions and submit their applications as early as possible.

What Is the BRAC Regular Internship Programme?

The BRAC Regular Internship programme provides opportunities for individuals to gain hands-on experience within different functions of BRAC and its affiliated programmes and organisations.

BRAC operates across a broad range of development areas, and its internship opportunities can expose participants to real-world organisational, financial, technological, social-impact and development-related work.

Rather than simply providing classroom-based learning, an internship with BRAC can allow participants to understand how a large development organisation operates and how different departments contribute to its overall mission.

Depending on the specific internship, participants may work alongside professionals in areas such as:

  • Human resources and talent acquisition
  • Executive and organisational support
  • Microfinance
  • Operations and strategy
  • Climate and environmental programmes
  • Information technology
  • Finance and accounting
  • Treasury operations
  • Development and social-impact programmes

The exact responsibilities, qualifications, duration, location and other conditions vary according to the individual internship position.

Current BRAC Internship Opportunities

1. BRAC International – Talent Acquisition, Human Resources

Application deadline: August 22, 2026

The BRAC International Talent Acquisition internship is focused on the Human Resources function.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in:

  • Human resource management
  • Recruitment and talent acquisition
  • Employee engagement
  • Organisational development
  • People management
  • International development organisations
  • Administrative and HR operations

An internship in talent acquisition can provide valuable exposure to the processes organisations use to identify, attract and support qualified employees.

Candidates interested in building careers in human resources, recruitment or organisational management may find this opportunity particularly useful.

Official internship description: BRAC International – Talent Acquisition, Human Resources

2. BRAC International – Executive Director’s Office

Application deadline: August 22, 2026

BRAC International is also offering an internship opportunity within the Executive Director’s Office.

An internship in an executive office can provide exposure to organisational leadership, coordination, administration, strategic initiatives and high-level institutional operations.

Depending on the specific responsibilities outlined in the internship description, candidates may gain insight into how senior leadership functions within a major international development organisation.

This opportunity could be especially relevant to candidates interested in:

  • International development
  • Public administration
  • Business management
  • Leadership
  • Strategy
  • Executive support
  • Organisational coordination
  • Nonprofit management

Official internship description: BRAC International – Executive Director’s Office

3. Microfinance – Progoti

Application deadline: August 24, 2026

BRAC’s Microfinance – Progoti internship provides an opportunity to gain experience within one of the organisation’s microfinance-related areas.

Microfinance plays an important role in expanding access to financial services for people and businesses that may have limited access to traditional financial institutions.

An internship in this area can be particularly valuable for candidates interested in:

  • Finance
  • Banking
  • Microfinance
  • Financial inclusion
  • Business development
  • Economics
  • Development studies
  • Operations
  • Social entrepreneurship

Candidates interested in understanding how financial services can contribute to economic empowerment and development may find this internship particularly relevant.

Official internship description: Microfinance – Progoti

4. Climate Bridge Fund (CBF) Secretariat

Application deadline: August 26, 2026

The Climate Bridge Fund Secretariat internship provides an opportunity for candidates interested in climate action, development finance, sustainability and environmental issues.

Climate change is increasingly connected to economic development, livelihoods, financing, resilience and social protection. An internship within a climate-focused initiative can therefore provide exposure to the practical work involved in addressing climate-related development challenges.

This opportunity may be particularly suitable for candidates interested in:

  • Climate change
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Development studies
  • Climate finance
  • Sustainable development
  • International development
  • Research
  • Programme management
  • Policy
  • Environmental programmes

Candidates seeking careers at the intersection of climate and development may find this internship especially valuable.

Official internship description: Climate Bridge Fund Secretariat

5. Microfinance – Operational Strategy and Implementation (Dabi)

Application deadline: August 26, 2026

Another current internship opportunity is available within Microfinance – Operational Strategy and Implementation (Dabi).

The position is connected to operational strategy and implementation, making it potentially relevant to candidates interested in understanding how large-scale financial and development programmes are designed, coordinated and implemented.

The internship may be particularly useful for candidates pursuing professional interests in:

  • Operations management
  • Strategy
  • Microfinance
  • Finance
  • Business administration
  • Development management
  • Programme implementation
  • Project management
  • Economics
  • Financial inclusion

The opportunity can provide an avenue for interns to gain practical exposure to the operational side of development-focused financial services.

Official internship description: Microfinance – Operational Strategy and Implementation (Dabi)

6. Technology – IT HelpDesk

Application deadline: August 29, 2026

BRAC is also accepting applications for an internship within its Technology – IT HelpDesk function.

This opportunity is particularly relevant to candidates interested in information technology and technical support.

An IT HelpDesk environment can provide practical experience with organisational technology systems and the processes involved in supporting users and maintaining effective technology operations.

Candidates interested in areas such as the following may consider this opportunity:

  • Information technology
  • Computer science
  • IT support
  • Technical support
  • Information systems
  • Networking
  • Technology operations
  • Digital services

The internship can be useful for students or early-career professionals seeking practical experience to complement their academic training in technology-related disciplines.

Official internship description: Technology – IT HelpDesk

7. Finance and Accounts – Treasury

Application deadline: August 31, 2026

The Finance and Accounts – Treasury internship has the latest deadline among the currently listed opportunities, with applications closing on August 31, 2026.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in financial management and treasury functions.

Treasury operations are important to organisations because they involve managing financial resources, liquidity and other aspects of an institution’s financial operations.

Candidates interested in:

  • Finance
  • Accounting
  • Treasury
  • Banking
  • Economics
  • Financial management
  • Business administration
  • Investment and financial operations

may find this internship relevant to their career development.

Official internship description: Finance and Accounts – Treasury

Why Consider a BRAC Internship?

An internship with BRAC can provide more than an entry on a résumé. It can offer practical exposure to the operations of a major development organisation and help participants connect academic knowledge with real workplace responsibilities.

Some potential benefits include:

1. Practical Professional Experience

Interns can gain experience working within an established organisation and learn how professional teams manage projects, programmes and institutional responsibilities.

2. Exposure to International Development

BRAC is widely recognised for its work in development and social impact. Internships within its different programmes can help candidates understand how development initiatives are designed and implemented.

3. Career Development

Practical internship experience can strengthen a candidate’s résumé and demonstrate exposure to a professional working environment.

4. Department-Specific Experience

Because the current openings span multiple functions, candidates can pursue opportunities aligned with their academic background and career interests.

5. Understanding Organisational Operations

Interns can gain insight into how different teams, departments and programmes contribute to the functioning of a large organisation.

6. Opportunity to Apply Academic Knowledge

An internship can allow students and recent graduates to apply concepts learned through their academic programmes to practical workplace situations.

Who Can Apply for the BRAC Internships?

Eligibility varies according to the specific internship position. Applicants should therefore read the individual internship description carefully before applying.

The current opportunities are aimed at candidates whose academic background, skills and interests align with the relevant department.

Depending on the position, potentially relevant academic and professional backgrounds may include:

  • Business administration
  • Management
  • Finance
  • Accounting
  • Economics
  • Human resources
  • International development
  • Development studies
  • Environmental studies
  • Climate studies
  • Computer science
  • Information technology
  • Information systems
  • Public administration
  • Strategy and operations
  • Related disciplines

Applicants should not assume that studying one of these fields automatically makes them eligible. The precise academic qualifications, skills, experience and other requirements should be confirmed from the official description of each internship.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Identify the Right Internship

Review the seven currently open positions and determine which one best matches your academic background, skills and career goals.

Step 2: Read the Full Internship Description

Click the relevant official BRAC internship description and carefully review the responsibilities and eligibility requirements.

Step 3: Prepare Your Application

Prepare the documents and information requested by BRAC for the particular internship.

Ensure that your résumé or CV highlights experiences that are relevant to the position.

Step 4: Check the Deadline

The current deadlines range from August 22 to August 31, 2026.

Because the positions have different closing dates, applicants should pay attention to the deadline for the specific position they are applying for.

Step 5: Submit Through the Official Channel

Follow the application instructions provided by BRAC for the selected internship.

Applicants should avoid relying on third-party websites for final application instructions when the official BRAC posting is available.

Click HERE to learn more and apply for the BRAC Regular Internships 2026.

Current BRAC Internship Deadlines at a Glance

Internship Deadline
BRAC International – Talent Acquisition, Human Resources August 22, 2026
BRAC International – Executive Director’s Office August 22, 2026
Microfinance – Progoti August 24, 2026
Climate Bridge Fund (CBF) Secretariat August 26, 2026
Microfinance – Operational Strategy and Implementation (Dabi) August 26, 2026
Technology – IT HelpDesk August 29, 2026
Finance and Accounts – Treasury August 31, 2026

Application Tips for Prospective BRAC Interns

Applicants can improve their preparation by following several practical steps.

Match Your Application to the Position

Do not use exactly the same résumé or application approach for every internship. Emphasise the experiences and skills most relevant to the specific department.

Highlight Practical Skills

If applying for an HR position, for example, highlight recruitment, administration, communication or people-management experience. For a technology position, emphasise relevant technical skills and projects.

Demonstrate Relevant Academic Knowledge

Connect your academic background to the responsibilities of the internship where appropriate.

Apply Before the Deadline

Do not wait until the final hours. The earliest deadlines are August 22, 2026, meaning applicants interested in the BRAC International positions have very little time remaining.

Verify the Official Requirements

The general internship page does not replace the individual job description. Always check the official PDF for the position you intend to apply for.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this a single BRAC internship?

No. The current BRAC Regular Internship page lists several separate internship opportunities across different departments and programmes.

What are the current application deadlines?

The remaining opportunities close between August 22 and August 31, 2026.

Are the internships open to everyone?

No. Eligibility varies according to the individual internship. Applicants must meet the requirements specified for the position they wish to apply for.

Can students apply?

Potentially, depending on the requirements of the individual internship. Candidates should review the specific internship description for academic and other eligibility requirements.

Can graduates apply?

Potentially, depending on the requirements of the individual position. The specific internship description should be consulted before applying.

Are all the internships in the same field?

No. The current openings cover Human Resources, executive support, microfinance, climate, technology and finance.

Are the expired internships still included?

No. This updated article removes the four opportunities whose deadlines were August 18, August 19 and August 20, 2026.

What is the latest deadline among the current opportunities?

The Finance and Accounts – Treasury internship has the latest listed deadline: August 31, 2026.

Conclusion

The BRAC Regular Internship 2026 programme currently offers several opportunities for students, graduates and early-career candidates to gain practical experience in areas ranging from human resources and executive support to microfinance, climate action, information technology and finance.

As of August 20, 2026, seven opportunities remain open, with application deadlines running from August 22 through August 31, 2026. Candidates should therefore act quickly, particularly those interested in the BRAC International positions closing on August 22.

The most important step is to identify an internship that genuinely matches your academic background and career objectives, read its official description carefully, confirm the location and eligibility requirements, and submit a complete application before the relevant deadline.

For the latest information and official application instructions, applicants should consult BRAC’s official Regular Internship page and the individual internship descriptions provided above.

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day (AIPD) “My IP Story” initiative invites African entrepreneurs, innovators, creators, institutions and business owners who have used intellectual property rights to create value and grow their initiatives to share their experiences.

Held under the theme “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem,” the 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day initiative seeks to recognise and highlight compelling stories from African individuals and entities that have successfully leveraged intellectual property (IP) to develop a business, strengthen an initiative, protect innovation or create commercial value.

Through “My IP Story,” participants have an opportunity to explain their intellectual property journey in a video of no more than five minutes. The story should demonstrate how intellectual property rights have contributed to their progress, what type of IP protection they have used, the benefits they have experienced, and how the evolving intellectual property ecosystem associated with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) could further support their business.

Interested storytellers must prepare their videos according to the specified guidelines and complete the official submission form by 31 August 2026.

About the 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day, also referred to as #2026AIPD, focuses attention on the role intellectual property can play in the growth and development of businesses across Africa.

The theme for the 2026 edition is:

“Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem”

The theme connects intellectual property with the opportunities emerging through the African Continental Free Trade Area. It encourages African entrepreneurs and organisations to consider not only how intellectual property has helped them create value to date, but also how an AfCFTA intellectual property rights ecosystem could contribute to their future business development.

Intellectual property can represent an important component of a business or initiative. Depending on the nature of the activity, intellectual property rights can help protect inventions, brands, creative works, designs and other valuable intellectual assets.

The “My IP Story” initiative brings this subject to life by focusing on the actual experiences of Africans who have used intellectual property as part of their entrepreneurial, commercial or organisational journeys.

What Is the 2026 AIPD “My IP Story” Initiative?

“My IP Story” is an initiative designed to recognise stories from African individuals and entities that have leveraged intellectual property to grow a business or develop an initiative relying on intellectual property rights (IPR).

Rather than simply describing intellectual property in theoretical terms, participants are expected to tell the story of their own journey.

The story should trace the participant’s experience from the beginning of their business or initiative through to the achievements they have made, while demonstrating the impact that intellectual property rights have had on their success.

This means a strong submission should explain both the journey and the results. Participants should be able to show how intellectual property became relevant to their work, the particular intellectual property right they used and how that protection or intellectual asset has helped them create value.

Who Is “My IP Story” Designed For?

The submission form provides two types of participation:

  • Individual
  • Institution

The initiative specifically seeks stories from African individuals or entities that have leveraged intellectual property to grow their businesses or develop initiatives that rely on intellectual property rights.

Potential storytellers could therefore include individuals or institutions with a genuine intellectual property story demonstrating how IP has contributed to value creation, business development or the success of an initiative.

Applicants should ensure that their submission is based on their actual experience and clearly communicates the role intellectual property has played in their journey.

What Should Participants Submit?

The central requirement of the 2026 AIPD “My IP Story” initiative is a video telling the participant’s intellectual property story.

Each participant must submit a video with a maximum duration of five minutes.

The video should provide enough information for viewers to understand the storyteller, their business or initiative, their intellectual property journey and the benefits they have experienced from using intellectual property rights.

The submission must also be clearly labelled.

According to the submission requirements, the online form accepts one supported video file with a maximum file size of 1 GB.

Participants should therefore check the duration, file size and labelling of their video before uploading it.

2026 AIPD My IP Story Video Guidelines

The organisers have provided specific guidelines outlining the information that should be addressed in the video.

Participants should use these points as a checklist when planning and recording their stories.

1. State Your Full Name

The storyteller should clearly provide their full name.

This helps identify the individual presenting the story and connects the video with the information supplied through the application form.

2. State Your Country of Origin

Participants must identify their country of origin.

Because the initiative focuses on African intellectual property stories, this information provides important geographical context for the storyteller and their business or initiative.

3. Explain How Intellectual Property Has Helped With Value Creation

A central part of the story should answer the question:

How has intellectual property been helpful for value creation?

Participants should explain the practical connection between their intellectual property and the value generated by their business or initiative.

Rather than simply mentioning that intellectual property exists, storytellers should aim to demonstrate what difference it has made to their journey.

Depending on the participant’s circumstances, this could involve discussing how intellectual property has supported the development, protection, recognition or commercialisation of something valuable within their business or initiative.

4. Identify the Intellectual Property Right Used

The video must explain which Intellectual Property Right was used.

Participants should clearly identify the relevant form of intellectual property protection or right connected with their story.

The precise right will depend on the storyteller’s own circumstances and intellectual property journey. The important requirement is that participants clearly communicate which intellectual property right played a role in the development of their business or initiative.

5. Explain How Beneficial the Intellectual Property Has Been

Participants are also expected to answer:

How beneficial has this intellectual property been so far?

This part gives storytellers an opportunity to demonstrate the impact intellectual property has had on their progress.

Where possible, participants should communicate the benefits clearly and practically. The objective is to help viewers understand why the intellectual property mattered and how it contributed to the storyteller’s achievements.

6. Discuss Your Awareness of the AfCFTA

The video should address whether the storyteller has heard about the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

This requirement connects the participant’s personal intellectual property experience with the broader theme of the 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day.

Participants should answer this component clearly within their video.

7. Explain How the AfCFTA IPR System Could Enhance Your Business

Participants should go beyond simply stating whether they are aware of AfCFTA.

They must also consider the question:

How could the AfCFTA IPR system enhance your business?

This is an important part of the submission because it directly relates the storyteller’s experience to the 2026 theme, “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem.”

Participants should consider their own business or initiative and explain how an intellectual property rights system within the AfCFTA context could potentially contribute to its future development.

The answer should ideally be connected to the participant’s actual business experience and future ambitions rather than being a general discussion disconnected from their story.

Rules for Songs and Voices Used in the Video

Participants who incorporate a song or voice into their submission must clearly mention the title and/or author of any song or voice used.

This requirement should not be overlooked when preparing the final video.

Before submitting, participants should review the entire recording and ensure that any song or voice included has been appropriately identified according to the submission guidelines.

What Language Can Be Used for the 2026 AIPD My IP Story?

The story must be presented in one of the African Union (AU) languages.

Participants should ensure their chosen language complies with this requirement before recording and submitting the final video.

Because language is an explicit part of the guidelines, applicants should not assume that a video in any language will automatically qualify. The story should be delivered using an AU language.

Required Information on the Application Form

In addition to uploading the video, applicants must provide several pieces of information through the official submission form.

The required fields listed on the form include:

  1. Email
  2. Full name of the storyteller
  3. Type of submission
  4. Email address of the storyteller
  5. Country of origin of the storyteller
  6. Short description of the business or initiative
  7. Video submission

For the type of submission, participants can select:

  • Individual
  • Institution

The video must be uploaded through the submission form and should be clearly labelled.

Video Technical Requirements

Participants should pay close attention to the technical requirements before completing their application.

The submitted video must meet the following conditions:

  • The video must be no longer than five minutes.
  • Only one video file can be uploaded through the specified upload field.
  • The maximum permitted file size is 1 GB.
  • The video submission must be clearly labelled.
  • The story must comply with the specified content requirements.
  • The story must be delivered in one of the AU languages.
  • Any applicable song or voice used should have its title and/or author clearly mentioned.

Applicants should review the completed video against all of these requirements before uploading it.

How to Prepare a Strong My IP Story

While participants should remain faithful to their own experiences and the official requirements, planning the video before recording can make it easier to cover all of the requested information within the five-minute limit.

A practical structure could be:

Opening: Introduce Yourself

Begin by clearly stating:

  • Your full name
  • Your country of origin
  • Your business or initiative
  • What the business or initiative does

The introduction should establish enough context for viewers to understand the rest of the story.

Explain Your Journey

Describe how the business or initiative began.

This is where the participant can provide the background necessary to understand why intellectual property became relevant.

The initiative specifically seeks stories reflecting the journey from the onset to the achievement, so participants should consider explaining where they started, what they developed and how their intellectual property journey evolved.

Introduce the Intellectual Property

Clearly explain:

  • The intellectual property involved
  • Which intellectual property right was used
  • Why it was relevant to the business or initiative

Avoid leaving the audience to guess what type of intellectual property is at the centre of the story.

Explain the Value Created

Describe how intellectual property contributed to value creation.

This is one of the most important components of the submission because “My IP Story” is intended to recognise experiences in which intellectual property has been leveraged for business growth or initiative development.

Describe the Benefits

Explain the benefits that the intellectual property has produced so far.

Participants should focus on their actual experience and achievements.

Address AfCFTA

Explain whether you have heard about AfCFTA and then discuss how you believe the AfCFTA IPR system could enhance your business.

Connecting this part of the video directly to your own business or initiative can help maintain a coherent story.

Review Before Submission

Before uploading the video, check that every required topic has been addressed and that the video does not exceed five minutes.

Also verify the language, file size, file labelling and any required attribution for songs or voices used.

Suggested Pre-Submission Checklist

Before completing the online form, participants should verify that they have:

  • Prepared a video of no more than five minutes.
  • Clearly stated the storyteller’s full name.
  • Clearly stated the storyteller’s country of origin.
  • Explained how intellectual property has contributed to value creation.
  • Identified the Intellectual Property Right used.
  • Explained how beneficial the intellectual property has been.
  • Addressed whether the storyteller has heard about the AfCFTA.
  • Explained how the AfCFTA IPR system could enhance the business.
  • Identified the title and/or author of any song or voice used, where applicable.
  • Presented the story in one of the AU languages.
  • Clearly labelled the video submission.
  • Confirmed that the video file is no larger than 1 GB.
  • Prepared a short description of the business or initiative for the application form.
  • Confirmed that all required form fields are complete.
  • Prepared to submit everything before the deadline.

2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day My IP Story Deadline

The official submission deadline is 31 August 2026.

Prospective participants should aim to prepare, review and upload their video before the final day rather than waiting until the deadline.

Deadline: 31 August 2026

Applicants should ensure that the complete submission, including the required information and video upload, is successfully submitted through the official form by the deadline.

APPLY NOW

Why the 2026 AIPD Theme Matters for African Businesses

The theme “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem” places intellectual property within the wider conversation about business growth and economic integration across Africa.

For entrepreneurs and organisations, intellectual property can be more than a legal concept. Brands, inventions, designs, creative works and other intellectual assets can form an important part of how an enterprise creates and protects value.

“My IP Story” provides a platform for these experiences to be communicated through the voices of the people and entities that have actually used intellectual property.

By asking participants to discuss both their past experiences with IP and their expectations of the AfCFTA IPR system, the initiative also encourages storytellers to consider how intellectual property could support their future growth within an increasingly connected African market.

Important Information Before Submitting

Participants should carefully review the submission form and requirements before uploading their files.

The Google Form states that the name, email address and photo associated with the Google account used to submit the form will be recorded when files are uploaded and the form is submitted.

Applicants should therefore make sure they are signed into the appropriate Google account before completing their submission.

The form also warns users never to submit passwords through Google Forms.

Conclusion

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day “My IP Story” initiative offers African individuals and entities an opportunity to tell the story behind the intellectual property that has contributed to their business or initiative.

Under the theme “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem,” participants are encouraged to demonstrate how intellectual property has helped them create value, identify the intellectual property right they have used, describe the benefits it has delivered and consider how the AfCFTA intellectual property rights ecosystem could further enhance their business.

The submission takes the form of a maximum five-minute video, supported by information about the storyteller and their business or initiative. Participants must follow the content requirements carefully, use one of the AU languages, appropriately identify songs or voices where applicable, clearly label their video and ensure the uploaded file does not exceed 1 GB.

African entrepreneurs, innovators, creators and institutions with a meaningful intellectual property journey should carefully review the requirements and prepare their stories ahead of time.

The deadline to submit a 2026 AIPD My IP Story is 31 August 2026.

item.content:encoded:
UNICEF Ghana is inviting talented young filmmakers and animators to turn powerful ideas about children into compelling visual stories through its Call for Young Filmmakers and Animators. The opportunity provides GHS 10,000 in production support to help selected young creatives develop and produce an original short film or animation centered on children’s rights and experiences.

The call presents an important opportunity for emerging filmmakers and animators who believe in the power of storytelling to amplify children’s voices, represent their experiences and encourage greater awareness of the issues affecting children.

Young creatives between 18 and 35 years old who can tell an engaging children’s story in five minutes or less are encouraged to consider applying.

For filmmakers and animators who have a compelling creative concept but need financial support to bring it to life, the UNICEF Ghana production support could provide the resources needed to transform that concept into a finished visual story.

About the UNICEF Ghana Call for Young Filmmakers and Animators

UNICEF works globally to advance and protect the rights of children, including supporting efforts that help children grow up healthy, educated, protected from harm and able to reach their full potential.

Storytelling can play an important role in that mission. Films and animations can make complex issues understandable, create emotional connections with audiences and provide opportunities for children’s experiences and perspectives to be represented.

Through this call, UNICEF Ghana is looking for young filmmakers and animators who can use their creativity to develop an original story focusing on children’s rights and experiences.

The central challenge is straightforward: applicants should be able to tell a captivating children’s story through film or animation in no more than five minutes.

Successful applicants can receive GHS 10,000 in production support to develop and produce their proposed work.

GHS 10,000 in Production Support

One of the most significant features of the UNICEF Ghana opportunity is the financial support available to successful applicants.

UNICEF Ghana states that young filmmakers and animators can apply for:

GHS 10,000 in production support

The funding is intended to support the development and production of an original short film or animation.

For an emerging creative, production funding can make an important difference. Producing even a short film or animation can involve expenses associated with equipment, production, post-production, creative services and other resources required to transform an idea into a completed project.

The UNICEF Ghana call therefore offers more than an invitation to share an idea. It provides successful applicants with tangible production support to help bring their creative concepts to life.

What Kind of Film or Animation Is UNICEF Ghana Looking For?

Applicants should pay particularly close attention to the subject and length of the proposed project.

UNICEF Ghana is seeking an original short film or animation focused on children’s rights and experiences.

The proposed story should therefore meaningfully connect with children and the realities, rights, voices or experiences that affect them.

The call emphasizes several important elements:

  1. The work should be original.
    Applicants are being invited to develop and produce an original short film or animation rather than simply submit an unrelated existing creative project.
  2. The story should focus on children.
    Children’s rights and experiences should be central to the proposed production.
  3. The story should be engaging.
    UNICEF Ghana specifically asks whether applicants can tell a captivating children’s story, indicating that strong storytelling will be an important element of the project.
  4. The final story should be short.
    Applicants should be able to communicate their story in five minutes or less.
  5. Children’s voices and rights should be meaningfully represented.
    The opportunity emphasizes the importance of children seeing their stories, voices and rights represented through film or animation.

This means applicants should think beyond simply producing visually impressive content. The story itself should have a clear connection to children and should be capable of communicating that message effectively within a very short format.

Who Can Apply for the UNICEF Ghana Young Filmmakers and Animators Opportunity?

The call is specifically directed toward young filmmakers and animators between the ages of 18 and 35.

Potential applicants should consider whether they meet the core characteristics highlighted by UNICEF Ghana.

Applicants should:

  • Be between 18 and 35 years old.
  • Be a filmmaker or animator, or have a strong passion for filmmaking or animation.
  • Have a compelling story or creative idea to share.
  • Be capable of developing an engaging children’s story.
  • Be able to tell the proposed story in five minutes or less.
  • Be interested in representing children’s stories, voices, rights and experiences through film or animation.
  • Have an original short-film or animation concept focused on children’s rights and experiences.
  • Be interested in receiving production support to develop and produce the project.

The published announcement supplied for this opportunity does not specify a university degree, particular academic qualification or minimum number of years of professional filmmaking experience.

This makes it particularly important for interested young creatives to focus on the quality, originality and relevance of their proposed story while carefully reviewing the official application form for any additional conditions.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be between:

18 and 35 years old.

Anyone considering the opportunity should ensure they satisfy the age requirement before beginning the application process.

Maximum Film or Animation Length

Another major requirement concerns the duration of the proposed production.

The applicant must be capable of telling the children’s story in:

Five minutes or less.

This requirement makes concise storytelling particularly important.

A five-minute film does not provide unlimited time to establish characters, communicate a message and conclude a story. Applicants will therefore need to think carefully about the structure and focus of their concept.

A strong proposal should have a clear central idea and avoid unnecessary complexity that would make it difficult to communicate the story effectively within the required duration.

Focus on Children’s Rights and Experiences

The proposed short film or animation should focus on children’s rights and experiences.

UNICEF’s broader work is centered on advancing children’s rights and protecting children from harm and discrimination while supporting their health, education, development and ability to reach their potential.

For applicants, this means the proposed project should maintain a meaningful connection to children rather than using children merely as background characters.

The announcement particularly emphasizes the importance of children seeing their:

  • Stories represented;
  • Voices represented;
  • Rights represented; and
  • Experiences reflected through film or animation.

Applicants should therefore consider how their proposed story can meaningfully place children’s experiences at its center.

Why This Opportunity Matters for Young Filmmakers and Animators

Short films and animations can be powerful communication tools because they combine storytelling with visual expression.

For emerging filmmakers and animators, however, transforming an idea into a completed production can require resources that may not always be readily available.

UNICEF Ghana’s GHS 10,000 production support provides successful applicants with financial assistance specifically intended to help develop and produce their original project.

The opportunity can be particularly valuable for young creatives who already have an idea connected to children’s experiences but need production support to turn that idea into a finished film or animation.

It also provides an opportunity for young storytellers to direct their creative abilities toward issues affecting children.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Successful applicants can receive:

GHS 10,000 in Production Support

The support is intended to help applicants develop and produce an original short film or animation.

Applicants should understand that this is described specifically as production support. They should therefore carefully review any additional instructions in the official application form regarding how the funding may be used and whether successful applicants will have additional production, reporting or delivery requirements.

What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying

Before submitting an application, interested filmmakers and animators should make sure their concept responds directly to the purpose of the call.

A useful pre-application checklist includes the following:

  • Is the applicant between 18 and 35 years old?
  • Is the proposed project a film or animation?
  • Is the story original?
  • Does the concept focus meaningfully on children?
  • Does it represent children’s rights, voices or experiences?
  • Can the story be communicated effectively in five minutes or less?
  • Is the idea engaging enough to work as a short visual story?
  • Is the concept realistic enough to be developed and produced with the available support?
  • Has the applicant reviewed the official application form for any additional requirements?

Answering these questions before applying can help applicants determine whether their concept aligns with the opportunity.

How to Apply

Applications are being accepted through the official UNICEF Ghana application form hosted on Microsoft Forms.

Interested applicants should use the official application link provided by UNICEF Ghana:

Application form: https://forms.office.com/e/0bT2ZFyAw4

Applicants should carefully read all questions and instructions presented in the application form before submitting their information.

Because the supplied public announcement contains only a brief overview of the call, the application form may contain additional questions or requirements that are not reproduced in the announcement.

Applicants should therefore rely on the official UNICEF Ghana page and application form for the final requirements governing their submission.

APPLY NOW

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the supplied UNICEF Ghana announcement.

Applicants should not assume that the opportunity will remain open indefinitely. Anyone interested in the GHS 10,000 production support should check the official UNICEF Ghana opportunity page and application form for the latest information regarding the closing date and submit as early as reasonably possible.

If a deadline appears within the application form, applicants should follow that deadline.

Important Details at a Glance

  • Organizing organization: UNICEF Ghana
  • Opportunity: Call for Young Filmmakers and Animators
  • Production support: GHS 10,000
  • Target applicants: Young filmmakers and animators
  • Age requirement: 18–35 years
  • Project format: Short film or animation
  • Maximum duration: Five minutes or less
  • Main theme: Children’s rights and experiences
  • Creative emphasis: Children’s stories, voices and rights
  • Application method: Online application through the official Microsoft Forms link
  • Deadline: Not stated in the supplied announcement

Tips for Developing a Strong Creative Concept

Although the supplied UNICEF announcement does not provide a detailed judging rubric, applicants can still strengthen their preparation by ensuring that their proposal responds closely to the purpose of the call.

1. Start With a Clear Story

A short film has limited time to communicate its message. The central story should therefore be easy for an audience to understand.

Applicants should be able to explain what happens, whose story is being told and why that story matters.

2. Keep Children at the Center

The opportunity is specifically focused on children’s rights and experiences.

The creative concept should therefore demonstrate a meaningful understanding of the child-focused nature of the call.

3. Think Visually

Film and animation are visual storytelling formats.

Applicants should consider how characters, environments, movement, sound and visual composition can communicate aspects of the story rather than relying entirely on dialogue or narration.

4. Respect the Five-Minute Limit

A concept that requires 20 or 30 minutes to explain may be difficult to adapt effectively to the required format.

Applicants should consider whether the core story can genuinely be introduced, developed and concluded within five minutes.

5. Make the Idea Original

UNICEF Ghana specifically refers to the development and production of an original short film or animation.

Applicants should therefore bring their own creative perspective to the subject.

6. Connect Creativity With Children’s Rights and Experiences

A visually attractive production alone may not address the central purpose of the opportunity.

Applicants should ensure that the connection to children’s experiences, voices or rights is meaningful and visible in the proposed story.

About UNICEF Ghana

UNICEF works to uphold the rights of children and protect them from harm and discrimination while supporting conditions that allow them to grow up healthy, educated and capable of reaching their full potential.

UNICEF Ghana carries this broader mandate into its work within Ghana while supporting national priorities affecting children.

The Young Filmmakers and Animators call brings creative storytelling into this child-rights mission by encouraging young creatives to develop visual stories through which children’s experiences and perspectives can be represented.

Why You Should Consider Applying

For young filmmakers and animators, this opportunity combines creative storytelling with the possibility of receiving direct production support.

Successful applicants could receive GHS 10,000 to help turn an original idea into a short film or animation.

The opportunity may be particularly relevant if you:

  • Are between 18 and 35 years old;
  • Have an interest or background in filmmaking or animation;
  • Have an original story involving children;
  • Care about children’s voices, experiences and rights;
  • Can communicate that story effectively in five minutes or less; and
  • Need production support to help transform the concept into a finished creative work.

Rather than leaving a promising story as an undeveloped idea, this call provides young creatives with an opportunity to seek support to bring that story to life.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Ghana Call for Young Filmmakers and Animators offers young creatives an opportunity to combine filmmaking or animation with meaningful storytelling about children.

Young filmmakers and animators aged 18 to 35 are invited to propose an original short film or animation focused on children’s rights and experiences, with the story designed to run for five minutes or less.

Successful applicants can receive GHS 10,000 in production support to help develop and produce their creative project.

For young storytellers who believe children deserve to see their experiences, voices and rights meaningfully represented on screen, this opportunity provides a practical pathway for turning an idea into a production.

The supplied UNICEF Ghana announcement does not state an application deadline, so prospective applicants should check the official opportunity page and application form for the latest closing-date information and any additional requirements.

Interested applicants should review the official information carefully and submit their application through UNICEF Ghana’s designated application form.

Apply here: https://forms.office.com/e/0bT2ZFyAw4

Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is currently recruiting for three positions in the United Kingdom, offering opportunities for professionals and candidates interested in working with an international organization.

The current vacancies include roles in visa application support, an internship at the Korean Visa Application Center, and external relations. Applicants should review the requirements for each position carefully and ensure that their IOM candidate profile is complete before submitting an application.

Current IOM Job Vacancies

According to the vacancy information provided, there are currently three open positions:

Position Location Application Deadline
Visa Support Assistant (KVAC) United Kingdom 1st September2026
Korean Visa Application Center (KVAC) Intern United Kingdom 1st September 2026
Senior External Relations Associate United Kingdom 27 August 2026

Important: The source lists the first two deadlines as 09/01/2026. Because the date format is not explicitly explained in the provided material, applicants should verify the exact closing date on the official IOM vacancy page before applying.

1. Visa Support Assistant (KVAC)

The Visa Support Assistant (KVAC) is one of the current vacancies listed by IOM in the United Kingdom.

The position is associated with the Korean Visa Application Center (KVAC) and is therefore relevant to candidates interested in visa application services and administrative support.

Key information

  • Organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
  • Position: Visa Support Assistant (KVAC)
  • Location: United Kingdom
  • Type: Job
  • Deadline listed: 9 January 2026

Applicants should consult the specific vacancy announcement for the detailed educational, professional and other eligibility requirements before applying.

2. Korean Visa Application Center (KVAC) Intern

IOM is also advertising an internship position at the Korean Visa Application Center (KVAC) in the United Kingdom.

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to candidates looking to gain professional experience within an international organization and a visa application centre environment.

Key information

  • Organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
  • Position: Korean Visa Application Center (KVAC) Intern
  • Location: United Kingdom
  • Type: Internship
  • Deadline listed: 9 January 2026

The provided vacancy listing does not contain the detailed qualification requirements for this internship. Candidates should therefore check the individual vacancy announcement for the complete eligibility criteria.

3. Senior External Relations Associate

The third vacancy is for a Senior External Relations Associate in the United Kingdom.

This is a more experienced-level opportunity and may be suited to candidates with a professional background relevant to external relations and related areas.

Key information

  • Organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
  • Position: Senior External Relations Associate
  • Location: United Kingdom
  • Type: Job
  • Deadline: 27 August 2026

Applicants should review the individual job description for the complete requirements, including education, professional experience and any position-specific qualifications.

Why Consider an IOM Career Opportunity?

Working with IOM can provide candidates with the opportunity to contribute to the work of an international organization.

The current vacancies cover different career levels and functions, meaning that candidates with different professional interests may find an opportunity relevant to their background.

The three vacancies span:

  • Visa support services
  • Internship and professional development
  • External relations

Candidates should focus on the specific requirements of the position they are interested in rather than assuming that eligibility for one vacancy automatically applies to another.

How to Apply for IOM Vacancies

IOM provides an online recruitment platform where candidates can create and manage their profiles and apply for vacancies.

Before applying, candidates are encouraged to:

  1. Create or update their IOM candidate profile.
  2. Complete their education information.
  3. Complete their professional work experience.
  4. Review the requirements of the specific vacancy.
  5. Prepare the required application materials.
  6. Submit the application before the applicable deadline.

IOM specifically warns that incomplete candidate profiles can affect eligibility.
